headline: Membership economics widening across platforms, toll enabling multiplier monetization.

deltas.metric: subscription services vs third-party seller services leverage
deltas.reads: membership toll gates customers into ecosystem where adjacent monetization surfaces (seller fees, ads, fast delivery) scale far faster than subscription revenue itself
membership sustains high-frequency consumer habit while marketplace monetization (merchant fees, advertising) compounds on top of the same captive customer base

deltas.metric: subscription base to advertising layer expansion
deltas.from: 2025 full year: ad revenue $1.5B+; 325M+ paid members
deltas.to: 2026 full year on track: ad revenue $3B; 325M+ members across quarters
deltas.change: ad revenue $3B vs subscription pricing power stable; ~2x ad revenue growth
deltas.reads: membership foundation enables growing advertising monetization without losing core subscriber retention or pricing leverage

deltas.from: 2025: net card fee revenue 30th straight quarter of double-digit growth
deltas.to: 2Q26: U.S. consumer spend +11%; 70%+ of new accounts on fee-paying products
deltas.change: +11% consumer spend YoY; fee-paying product mix hardening
deltas.reads: membership tolls convert consumers into higher-tier fee-paying card holders, unlocking merchant network, travel ecosystem, and purchase-behavior monetization

deltas.from: Q3 2025: 84% of net sales from Autoship; 21M active customers
deltas.to: Q1 2026: gross margin +50bp to 30.1%; 21.3M active customers; record quarterly profitability
deltas.change: +50bp margin expansion; steady member growth with improved unit economics
deltas.reads: membership (autoship) converts one-time pet product purchase into recurring revenue stream and health/wellness service attachment, enabling margin expansion

deltas.metric: loyalty member booking concentration to co-brand fee economics
deltas.from: 2025: 75% of U.S. room nights booked by Bonvoy members
deltas.to: Q1 2026: co-branded card fees +$60M; worldwide RevPAR +4.2%
deltas.change: +$60M card-fee contribution YoY; loyalty member concentration stable and high
deltas.reads: membership toll gates travel behavior into branded system where payment products and loyalty-funded distribution reinforce owner signings and occupancy growth

deltas.metric: membership pricing power and member base
deltas.from: 2025: 20.8M members after 50% price increase to new Classic Card; +1.1M net member growth
deltas.to: Q2 2026: 21.5M+ members (Q1); same-club sales growth moderate but retained after pricing test
deltas.change: tolerated 50% price increase and retained growth; full-year revenue +12.1%
deltas.reads: membership fee structure shows pricing power despite affordability positioning; member base stickiness indicates toll is internalized as essential recurring habit

momentum_note: Membership economics are accelerating across consumer platforms, but not through higher membership fees alone. The trend shows a shift from membership as a standalone revenue line to membership as a toll that gates customers into tiered monetization ecosystems. Amazon layers seller fees and advertising on top of Prime; Netflix is doubling advertising revenue while keeping subscription base flat; DoorDash and Chewy are growing marketplace/recurring revenue 2-3x faster than membership growth; Marriott and AmEx are monetizing the same member through co-branded payments and premium tiers. The deltas show membership becoming structural infrastructure rather than a pricing mechanism—it enables higher-frequency customer behavior, supplier concentration, and adjacent revenue capture. Even Planet Fitness's pricing power and Bath & Body Works's loyalty-member stagnation reinforce the core thesis: the membership toll itself matters less than what platforms stack on top of it.
